title: Breaking the bicycle frame: Coset-based quantum LDPC codes
authors: Arda Aydin, Itzhak Tamo, Alexander Barg
abstract: Generalizing the construction of two-block group algebra (2BGA) codes, we introduce a family of two-block quantum LDPC codes constructed using the action of a group on the cosets of its subgroup. This replaces the regular group actions of the earlier two-block constructions and significantly expands the search space, yielding new quantum LDPC codes outside the 2BGA family. Through a computer search, we identify several new quantum LDPC codes, including weight-6 codes with parameters $[[48,8,6]]$, $[[96,8,10]]$, and $[[224,12,16]]$, as well as weight-8 codes with parameters $[[84,16,8]]$, $[[112,16,10]]$, $[[128,16,12]]$, and $[[168,16,15]]$. Furthermore, we introduce a maximally packed syndrome extraction schedule of depth $w+2$, including initialization and measurement steps, for any code with a maximum stabilizer weight of $w$ from our family. Under a standard circuit-level noise model, our codes, when decoded using BP-OSD, perform competitively with BB codes, achieving thresholds of $\approx0.65\%$ for the weight-6 family and $\approx0.35\%$ for the weight-8 family. Finally, we introduce a group-theoretic framework to generate sequences of graph-based covers of 2BGA codes, recovering and extending recent results on code constructions of this type.
summary: This paper introduces a generalized group-theoretic construction method for quantum LDPC codes by utilizing the action of a group on its cosets. This framework expands beyond previous constructions, yielding new high-performance codes whose parameters and noise thresholds are analyzed. The authors also provide systematic methods to build efficient syndrome extraction circuits for these novel codes.
main_problem: The primary goal is to construct novel quantum Low-Density Parity-Check (LDPC) codes that surpass the limitations of existing constructions, particularly those based on Two-Block Group Algebra (2BGA) codes.
main_result: A new coset-based construction method is introduced using group actions on cosets, yielding several concrete examples of high-performing quantum LDPC codes with parameters like [[48, 8, 6]].
method: The authors develop a general framework based on the action of a group G on the cosets of its subgroup H to define parity-check matrices for CSS quantum codes.
model_or_system: The model is theoretical: constructing fault-tolerant quantum error correction codes, specifically two-block CSS quantum LDPC codes defined by group algebra actions $Q^H_G(a, b)$.
key_observables: Code parameters $[[n, k, d]]$, achievable syndrome extraction circuit depth ($w+2$), and noise thresholds ($\approx 0.65\%$ for weight-6 family).
important_parameters: Group structures $(G, H)$, stabilizer weights ($w_a, w_b$), code length $n=2[G:H]$, and thickness $	heta$ of the Tanner graph.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on establishing planarity properties for subgraphs related to syndrome extraction cycles and assuming specific structural constraints on group elements to simplify the search space.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate relationships between various quantum LDPC codes (e.g., BB Code, ZSZ Code) and detail the structure of the wheel graph used in syndrome extraction analysis.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from introducing the general coset-based construction to deriving mathematical properties like thickness bounds using planarity arguments, systematically searching for new code examples, and finally detailing the circuit implementation for syndrome extraction.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful algebraic tool (group theory) to generate structured quantum codes, which is crucial for designing hardware-efficient error correction protocols in superconducting or trapped-ion platforms.
